title: Vendor / tool selection — Security incident & disclosure
transcript:
Security Lead: Alright, let's get started. On-call, I've been reviewing the incident response system options and I'd like to discuss our next steps.

On-call Engineer: Sure, I've gathered some insights from the team. We've considered CrowdStrike's CyberXDR, Alert Logic, and Tanium Incident Response.

Legal Counsel: Before we dive in, I'd like to raise a point about compliance. If we continue with Splunk, how will we address potential gaps in our compliance?

Security Lead: Valid concern, Legal. I've been in touch with our compliance team, and they've assured me that with proper configuration and maintenance, Splunk should meet our compliance needs.

Comms Lead: Given the potential for a breach, wouldn't switching to a new system help improve our public image?

Security Lead: Comms, I understand your point, but at this moment, we can't justify the additional cost or downtime that would come with switching to a new vendor.

On-call Engineer: If I may, I'd like to present the pros and cons of each option. CrowdStrike is robust but expensive, Alert Logic provides excellent feature fit and support quality but requires migration cost and downtime, while Tanium has lower migration costs but moderate feature fit compared to Splunk.

Legal Counsel: I appreciate the rundown, On-call, but I'm still concerned about the compliance aspect. Is there a way we can mitigate this risk?

Security Lead: I've been in touch with our vendors and I've been assured that Splunk can meet our compliance needs if properly configured and maintained.

Comms Lead: I understand the concerns, but I still believe that switching to a new system could help improve our public image in the event of a breach.

Security Lead: Comms, I understand your point, but we cannot justify the additional cost or downtime that would come with switching to a new vendor at this time.

On-call Engineer: I agree, Security Lead. Given our current budget constraints and the lack of a superior alternative, maintaining the status quo with our existing incident response system seems to be the best option.

Legal Counsel: Alright, I'll need to revisit this issue when the budget is reviewed again next quarter.

Security Lead: Agreed, Legal. On-call, will you take ownership of this decision?

On-call Engineer: Of course, Security Lead. I'll work with the team to ensure our incident response system continues to serve us well.

Comms Lead: Understood, On-call. Let's hope we don't have to face a major security incident anytime soon.

On-call Engineer: Agreed, Comms. But if we do, I'll re-evaluate the need to upgrade or switch vendors.

Security Lead: Alright, that wraps up our discussion. On-call, can you send out a summary of our decision and next steps to everyone?

On-call Engineer: Absolutely, Security Lead. I'll send out the summary immediately.

(Off-topic exchange)

Comms Lead: By the way, On-call, have you seen the new coffee machine in the break room? It makes a mean latte!

On-call Engineer: Really? I haven't had a chance to check it out yet. I'll have to try it out sometime.

Security Lead: Alright, let's get back to business. On-call, please send out the summary. This meeting is adjourned.

On-call Engineer: Understood, Security Lead. I'll send out the summary immediately. Meeting adjourned.

(Security Lead signs off)
Security Lead: Meeting adjourned.

Title: Incident Response System Decision Record

Maintaining the status quo with the existing incident response system due to budget constraints and the lack of a clearly superior alternative. The annual cost of implementing CyberXDR by CrowdStrike exceeds our current fiscal year budget of $150,000. Given the insufficient evidence suggesting a substantial improvement over our current SIEM solution (Splunk), we cannot justify the additional cost or downtime associated with switching to a new vendor at this time. The on-call engineer will reassess the need to upgrade or switch vendors in the event of a major security incident.
